subject: Business Models
title: Platform Envelopment
description: A quick win: understand Platform Envelopment.

hook.text: Microsoft bundled Internet Explorer with Windows. Netscape went from 90% market share to dead.

buildup.text: Platform envelopment is when one platform extends into a competitor's territory using its existing user base.

discovery.text: Google launched Maps, Gmail, Drive, and Docs—enveloping features from dozens of standalone competitors.

twist.text: Apple launched Apple Pay, leveraging its billion iPhone users against established payment apps.

climax.text: Envelopment is the most common way big platforms kill smaller ones: absorb their features for free.

punchline.text: Bundle the competitor's product for free. Platform giants eat everyone.

quiz.question: What is platform envelopment?
options: Extending into rival territory using existing users

details.summary: Platform envelopment occurs when one platform uses its existing user base and capabilities to enter an adjacent market, absorbing a neighboring platform's functionality. Google expanding from search into maps, email, and office suites demonstrates envelopment strategy in action.
details.whyItMatters: Envelopment is how platform giants expand their empires. An established platform entering your market with bundled offerings and an existing user base is one of the most dangerous competitive threats a standalone platform can face.
takeaways: Established platforms enter adjacent markets using existing user bases
Bundling new functionality with existing services gives envelopers advantages
Envelopment is a primary growth strategy for platform conglomerates

faq.question: How does platform envelopment work as a competitive strategy?
faq.answer: A platform with a large user base in one market bundles functionality from an adjacent market into its existing product. Users adopt the new feature because it integrates seamlessly. The adjacent market's standalone competitor loses users who prefer the bundled solution.

faq.question: Can smaller platforms defend against envelopment by tech giants?
faq.answer: Defenses include deep specialization that generalists cannot match, community loyalty, superior user experience in the niche, regulatory protection, and building switching costs through data and workflow integration. Being acquired is also a common outcome.
